changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.lede: Every notable change to @2one/design-library, newest first — rendered live from the repository's CHANGELOG.md. Follows Keep a Changelog and Semantic Versioning.

hero.eyebrow: Design language system · delivered as a product
hero.body: Origin is a design language system for product development and product marketing — the components, tokens, brand, and the rules that bind them. A knowledge graph makes the system opinionated and deterministic, so people and AI build interfaces that already feel like 2one.

dlsTeaser.title: New here? Start with the DLS
dlsTeaser.body: A Design Language System is the shared kit — brand, tokens, components, and the rules that bind them. The guide explains the three tiers it’s built from and includes the live theming playground: set one brand colour and watch the whole system recolour, contrast-checked as you go.

features.title: What makes it different
features.lede: Each point below is a real capability with checkable evidence — no hype.

opinionated.title: Opinionated & deterministic
opinionated.desc: A knowledge graph of every token, component and rule — ask what a change touches before you ship it.

accessible.title: Accessible by default
accessible.desc: Radix primitives + an APCA contrast audit that runs on every change, in light and dark.

aiLegible.title: AI-legible
aiLegible.desc: Machine-readable UX rules with severity + precedence, so AI composes the 2one language — it doesn’t invent one.

universal.title: Universal & one system
universal.desc: One grayscale token system, two audited themes, semantic HTML — the same product feel on every surface.

use.title: How to use the application
use.lede: A step-by-step way to connect an AI assistant to the 2one library and build with it. Point your assistant — Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini — at the repo, have it read the system, then build from the real components, tokens and rules. No manual coding required.

step2.title: Ask for a summary first

faq.title: FAQ
faq.lede: The questions teams ask us when they first see the system — what it is, what you can build with it, how it’s licensed, and how an engagement works.

brand.q: Whose brand do we build with — ours or 2one’s?
brand.a: This repository is 2one’s own system: our brand, built on shadcn/ui, so our team ships product and marketing that already look like 2one. We share it so you can try the approach on something real. If it fits, we build the same foundations for your brand, wire them into your front-end library, and wrap an application around them for your team.

produce.q: What can our team actually produce with it?
produce.a: Websites, marketing pages and product screens — generated with AI against the system’s rules, so the output stays on-brand and carries fewer bugs. The same foundations live in Figma for designers and developers to share. It won’t hand you a finished application: it gives you a strong, consistent first version, and your team makes it their own.

who.a: The people deciding are product and engineering leaders — VPs, product managers, CXOs — who want their teams using AI productively, without the slop. The people using it day to day are developers, marketing teams and product managers who build against it.

shadcn.q: Is it tied to shadcn, and how is it licensed?
shadcn.a: No. shadcn is simply what 2one runs on; if your team is on MudBlazor, or anything else, we build the same system there. Licensing is yours to choose — open (MIT) by default, so anyone can clone and use it, or proprietary if you would rather keep it in-house.

access.a: Clone the repository and install the packages locally. Access is being opened up so there is nothing to set up — the people we share it with can pull it and start building. Today it is the foundation our team builds on; on the roadmap, a shared design system your whole organisation can draw from.

pyramid.aria: A three-tier pyramid: Tier 1 Brand at the top, Tier 2 Design Foundation in the middle, Tier 3 Design System at the base.

hero.body: A Design Language System (DLS) is the complete set of rules, assets, and principles that define how a brand looks, sounds, and behaves across every surface — from a mission statement to a product icon. It is organised into three tiers that move from strategic intent down to the finished work a customer sees.

glance.title: The three tiers, at a glance
glance.lede: The tiers can be read in either direction. Intent defined at the apex cascades down into everything the brand produces, and every finished asset at the base traces back up to the strategy that shaped it.
glance.row1Desc: Defines why the brand exists and who it serves. This tier is pure strategy and contains no visual rules; everything below must trace back to it.
glance.row2Desc: The reusable building blocks — colour, typography, iconography, and voice. This is the brand’s vocabulary; no element here is a finished deliverable.
glance.row3Desc: The building blocks assembled into finished, shippable work — applications, websites, decks, and campaigns. This is what customers ultimately see.

analogy.title: A working analogy: language
analogy.lede: The name is deliberate. A design language behaves much like a spoken one, and the three tiers map directly onto its structure.
analogy.card1Desc: Who you are addressing and what you mean to convey. This is the brand: mission, values, personality, and audience.
analogy.card2Desc: The words and rules you assemble sentences from. This is the design foundation: colour, typography, iconography, and tone of voice — reusable, never a finished sentence on their own.
analogy.card3Desc: The sentences you actually say. This is the design system in use: the product screens, websites, campaigns, and decks that customers experience.
analogy.construction: An alternative analogy is construction. Tier 1 is the project brief — what is being built and for whom; Tier 2 is the materials and the building code; and Tier 3 is the finished, occupied building.

tier1.title: Brand foundation — the “why” and “who”
tier1.lede: The strategic core of the system. This tier contains no visual rules; it defines why the brand exists and who it serves. Every decision in the tiers below must trace back to it.
tier1.appliedLede: Tier 1 for 2one itself — pulled from <mono>brand/brand.json</mono>, the source every on-brand asset traces back to.
tier1.voiceCardDesc: How the brand speaks — match this in any 2one-facing copy.
tier1.logoDesc: Two fills only — black on light, white on dark. Never recolour, rotate, or distort.

missionVision.title: Mission & Vision
missionVision.desc: The brand’s purpose today and its long-term aspiration — the reference point for every downstream decision.

values.title: Values
values.desc: The core principles that guide how the brand behaves and makes decisions.

personality.title: Personality
personality.desc: The brand’s human character — for example bold, precise, or approachable — which informs tone and visuals.

audiences.title: Audiences & Personas
audiences.desc: The defined segments the brand designs for, including their needs, behaviours, and context.

archetype.title: Archetype
archetype.desc: The brand’s narrative role — Hero, Sage, Creator, and so on — used to keep its character consistent.

tagline.title: Tagline
tagline.desc: A short, memorable line that captures the brand’s promise.

tier2.title: Design foundation — the building blocks
tier2.lede: The reusable building blocks and rules derived from Tier 1 — the brand’s vocabulary. No element in this tier is a finished deliverable; each is a rule or component that Tier 3 assembles into shipped work.

colours.title: Colours
colours.desc: The full colour system and the rules for using it — including accessibility.

typography.title: Typography
typography.desc: The type system — hierarchy, legibility and the voice of text.

iconography.title: Iconography
iconography.desc: A consistent icon system across product and marketing.

voice.title: Voice & Tone
voice.desc: How the brand sounds — the language equivalent of the visuals.

moodboard.title: Moodboard
moodboard.desc: Reference material that anchors abstract style in concrete examples.

tier3.title: Design system — the shipped output
tier3.lede: The applied layer, where the Tier 2 foundations are assembled into finished, shippable deliverables — organised by where they are used.

product.title: Product & Software
product.desc: Digital interfaces where the system becomes functional UI.

marketing.title: Marketing
marketing.desc: Outward-facing materials for growth and engagement.

principle.title: Human-understandable and AI-legible
principle.lede: A well-built DLS is documented clearly enough for a person to apply by hand, and structured precisely enough for an AI system to parse and build from without ambiguity.
principle.humanDesc: Every rule, token, and asset is documented in plain language, so a new team member can produce on-brand work without a designer present.
principle.aiTitle: An AI can build from it
principle.aiDesc: Every element is labelled and structured, so an AI assistant can read the system and generate on-brand work directly — without inventing colours, fonts, or components.

inrepo.title: Where each tier lives in this library
inrepo.lede: <mono>@yokesh-2one/design-library</mono> implements this three-tier model directly. Each tier maps to specific files in the repository.
inrepo.tier1Desc: Brand strategy — mission, values, personality, and voice — is defined in brand/brand.json and brand/BRAND.md.
inrepo.tier2Desc: The building blocks — colour, typography, and spacing — are defined as tokens in tokens/ and consumed by the components in src/components/ui.
inrepo.tier3Desc: The assembled, shippable pieces — pre-composed blocks, charts, and AI build recipes — live in src/blocks and recipes/.
inrepo.aiDesc: A machine-readable index ties the system together. An AI assistant reads these files first, then builds only from the system.
